def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-.before:
**(b) Incident plane-wave reading.** As an additional model assumption of the
pair, adopt the **stationary elastic beam model**. Fix a **wave number**
$k>0$, read in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and a **direction** $d\in S^{2}$. The model
declares the **incident plane-wave reading**
$$u_{\mathrm{inc}}(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x}$$
with the **incident energy reading** $E:=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ in joules and
the **incident current density**
$$\mathbf j_{\mathrm{inc}}:=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\,d,$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ by clause (d)5 of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; this is the current density of
the pair $u=\cos(kd\cdot x)$, $v=\sin(kd\cdot x)$ computed in clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]. The model
declares the **incident flux density** (current per unit area) to be the
number $J_{\mathrm{inc}}:=\hbar k/m$, read in
$\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$.
def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-.after:
**(b) Incident plane-wave reading and declared density scale.** As an
additional model assumption of the pair, adopt the **stationary elastic beam
model**. Fix a **wave number** $k>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, a **direction**
$d\in S^2$, and an **incident number-density scale** $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$. This scale is an explicitly declared model normalization;
no numerical sample density or measured beam value is supplied. Retain the
unit-amplitude, dimensionless incident shape
$$u_{\mathrm{inc}}(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x},$$
with energy reading $E:=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$ in joules. The **physical incident
beam field** is $\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\,u_{\mathrm{inc}}$,
with unit $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$ and constant model number density
$|\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}|^2=n_{\mathrm{inc}}$. For a dimensionless unit-amplitude
shape $\psi$, write $\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]:=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\nabla\psi)$ for the mathematical current of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]. Its incident
value is $(\hbar k/m)d$, with velocity unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The model's
**physical number-current density** is the current of
$\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi$,
$$\mathbf j[\Phi]:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline\Phi\nabla\Phi)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi].$$
Thus the **incident current density** and **incident flux density** through a
plane normal to $d$ are
$$\mathbf j_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}d,\qquad J_{\mathrm{inc}}:=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}>0,$$
both in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)5. The mathematical
plane-wave current of the cited lemma remains the unit-shape computation;
the density factor supplies the declared physical beam normalization.

def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-.after:
$f_k$ remains the amplitude relative to the incident field, in metres.
Here $\Omega:=x/r$ is the **outgoing unit direction**, and the precise decay
of the remainder $\mathcal E$ is fixed by the existence theorem of this page.
The **scattered physical field** is
$\Phi_{\mathrm{sc}}:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}(\Psi-u_{\mathrm{inc}})$.
The physical scattered radial current density, obtained by applying the
quadratic current formula to this scattered component, is
$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\left(\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right)\qquad(r\to\infty),$$
in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ for the fixed declared density scale. The leading
unit-shape current is clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]; the current of
the remainder is controlled by the stationary theorem. The definition uses
the scattered component, with no assumption that incident/scattered
interference in the total field vanishes.

pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amp.before: [F4] **Current readings.** The radial current of a stationary wave with outgoing amplitude coefficient $f$ satisfies $j^{\mathrm{sc}}_{r}=(\hbar k/m)|f|^{2}/r^{2}$ for the exact outgoing field and the beam model reads cross sections as ratios of currents ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] clauses (c), (d)).
pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amp.after: [F4] **Unit-shape and physical current readings.** The mathematical current functional is $\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\nabla\psi)$. For the unit incident shape its value is $(\hbar k/m)d$, and for the exact outgoing shape $fe^{ikr}/r$ its radial value is $(\hbar k/m)|f|^2/r^2$ ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]] clause (c)). For the declared constant $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$, the beam model reads the physical field as $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi$, so the quadratic functional gives $\mathbf j[\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi]=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]$, and its cross sections are ratios with $J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] (b)-(d)).

pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amp.after:
4.1 By [F1] the unit-shape scattered field $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x}$ has radial mathematical current $(\hbar k/m)|f_k|^2/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ uniformly. Write $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=u+iv$; the physical field has real and imaginary parts $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u,\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v$. Since the scale is constant, its current is $(\hbar/m)[(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)
abla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)-(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)
abla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)]=n_{\mathrm{inc}}(\hbar/m)(u
abla v-v
abla u)$ by [F4]. Thus the physical scattered current is the display in (c), and the same calculation on the unit incident plane wave gives $J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m>0$. Dividing yields $\lim_{r	o\infty}r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}/J_{\mathrm{inc}}=|f_k|^2$. Smoothness and boundedness of $f_k$ on the sphere, with [F1]'s uniform error, give the finite total cross section $\sigma=\int_{S^2}|f_k|^2d\Omega$. The unit-shape amplitude stays in metres and the density cancels from both cross-section readings. This is (c). [F1, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amp.before:
- **Normalization.** The amplitude is dimensionless in the nondimensional
  variables of the cited theorem and has the dimension of length after

pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amp.after:
- **Normalization.** With physical coordinates $x$ in metres and $k$ in
  inverse metres, the unit-incident shape $\Psi$ is dimensionless, the reduced
  potential $W=(2m/\hbar^2)V$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and the displayed
  integral for $f_k$ has dimension length. The physical beam field
  $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$; its number currents
  are in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$. The common density factor cancels, leaving
  $d\sigma/d\Omega$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,sr^{-1}}$ independently of its value.
